title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act establishes a framework for measuring and reporting on AI capabilities across key sectors in China. It requires regular collection, analysis, and disclosure of AI development metrics to guide policy decisions and inform the public.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act establishes rules for the creation, use, and deployment of AI models, requiring developers to document how they work and disclose potential biases and risks. It also sets standards for safety testing, accountability, and transparency to ensure AI systems behave responsibly and protect users from harm.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill requires companies that develop or distribute artificial‑intelligence systems to provide detailed “functional bills of materials” – a clear list of the hardware, software, and data components that make up the AI product. By mandating this transparency, the legislation aims to improve accountability, safety, and oversight of AI technologies, while also covering related regulatory and industry‑supporting provisions.

title: Workforce for AI Trust Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Workforce for AI Trust Act seeks to build a skilled national workforce that can design, deploy, and oversee trustworthy AI systems. It emphasizes training, education, and collaboration between industry, academia, and government to ensure AI technologies are safe, reliable, and aligned with public values.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 aims to reduce the carbon and resource footprint of AI systems. It establishes regulations, reporting requirements, and incentives to encourage the development and deployment of more sustainable AI technologies.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to prevent AI companies from charging excessive prices for AI services and from manipulating wages for workers in the AI industry. It would enforce regulations and penalties to ensure fair pricing and fair wages.

title: FARM AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.
summary: The FARM AI Act of 2026 establishes guidelines for the use of artificial intelligence in agriculture, ensuring that AI technologies enhance farming efficiency while protecting farmers' data privacy and ensuring transparent decision-making. The legislation also requires that AI systems deployed in farming meet safety standards and that farmers receive training to responsibly integrate AI tools into their operations.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act encourages the rapid development and use of artificial intelligence technologies in banking, investing, and payments, while ensuring that consumer protection and market stability are not compromised. It establishes rules for transparency, risk management, and ethical AI practices to help regulators and firms work together responsibly.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act is designed to boost the use of artificial intelligence in banking and other financial sectors, encouraging new products and services that can improve efficiency and customer experience. It also establishes basic safeguards and regulatory guidelines to ensure that AI deployment remains safe, fair, and transparent while fostering continued innovation.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act is a legislative effort to build and support a workforce skilled in AI, aiming to boost innovation and competitiveness in the United States. It proposes programs, funding, and partnerships that train and retain AI professionals while encouraging collaboration between academia, industry, and government to advance AI research and development.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: This act bans the construction or operation of AI data centers on federal lands, preventing any such facilities from being established in these areas. The goal is to protect federal property and avoid using public land for commercial AI infrastructure.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to ensure students from kindergarten through 12th grade learn how to responsibly use and understand artificial intelligence. It sets guidelines for schools to provide AI-focused curriculum, teacher training, and resources so students are prepared for a future where AI is an everyday tool.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a proposed federal law that seeks to improve students’ understanding of artificial intelligence and prepare them for its use in everyday life. It outlines federal guidelines and funding for schools to integrate AI education into curricula, ensuring that students, teachers, and parents are equipped with the skills and knowledge to navigate an AI‑rich world.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a legislative framework designed to regulate the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence systems to ensure safety, transparency, and accountability. It sets out standards, risk assessment requirements, and oversight mechanisms that businesses and developers must follow to protect consumers and society from potential harms.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act seeks to guide schools in safely integrating AI technology into teaching practices. It proposes training for teachers, sets usage guidelines, and aims to protect student privacy while fostering innovative learning opportunities.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 establishes clear guidelines and safety standards for AI‑powered toys intended for children, ensuring they are secure, age‑appropriate, and free from harmful content. The act requires manufacturers to meet these safety criteria, disclose data collection practices, and report any incidents to protect young users.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives is affirming that every American—and especially each community affected by the building or running of an artificial‑intelligence data center—deserves the right to full transparency and local control. This policy calls for clear disclosure about data‑center projects and gives communities the authority to shape decisions that impact them.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 sets out rules and best practices for using AI technologies in programs that serve military veterans. It aims to protect veterans’ rights, ensure transparency, and promote ethical AI development and deployment in healthcare, benefits, and support services.

title: Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Act seeks to prevent the misuse of AI to create false narratives that could harm individuals or groups. It establishes regulations for content verification, accountability for AI developers, and enforcement mechanisms to protect against fabricated exploitation.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes a framework for studying and governing the use of artificial intelligence in the judicial system. It requires regular reporting, independent oversight, and guidelines to ensure that AI tools employed in courts are transparent, accurate, and fair.

title: A bill to require a report on the use of artificial intelligence with respect to access to unminimized information collected pursuant to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The bill requires federal agencies to report on how they use artificial intelligence to handle unminimized information collected under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. It also addresses related issues and aims to increase oversight of AI in intelligence operations.

title: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025 seeks to stop companies from using AI systems to secretly coordinate prices or other market‑behaving practices. It establishes rules for monitoring algorithmic behavior, gives regulators the power to investigate, and imposes penalties for any collusive activity discovered.

title: Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025 is a U.S. law designed to lessen reliance on Chinese AI technology and talent. It seeks to protect national security and foster domestic innovation by restricting the use of certain Chinese AI tools and supply chains.
